description:
The Gharaunda-Group Home for Adults Scheme is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India aimed at providing comprehensive support and care for adults with disabilities. 

The scheme was officially launched on 15th September 2021. 

It is part of the broader efforts by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment to enhance the quality of life for persons with disabilities in India. 

The primary objective of the Gharaunda scheme is to create a supportive environment where adults with disabilities can live with dignity and independence. 

The scheme aims to establish group homes across various states in India. 

The target is to set up at least 300 group homes by the year 2025. 

Each group home is designed to accommodate 10 to 15 adults with disabilities. 

The initiative focuses on providing not just shelter but also rehabilitation services, vocational training, and social integration. 

The benefits of the Gharaunda scheme include financial assistance to the group homes and support for operational costs. 

The Government provides a grant of ₹15 lakh for the establishment of each group home. 

Additionally, there is an annual operational cost support of ₹5 lakh per group home. 

This funding is aimed at ensuring that the homes can provide adequate facilities and services to the residents. 

Eligibility for the Gharaunda scheme is primarily focused on adults with disabilities aged 18 years and above. 

The scheme is open to individuals with various types of disabilities as defined under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016. 

There are no specific income criteria for the individuals residing in these group homes. 

However, the group homes themselves must be registered societies or non-governmental organizations. 

The application process for setting up a group home under the Gharaunda scheme involves several steps. 

First, the interested organization must submit a detailed project proposal to the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. 

The proposal should outline the objectives, operational plan, and budgetary requirements. 

Required documents include the registration certificate of the organization, a detailed project report, and a plan for the management of the group home. 

Once the proposal is submitted, it will be reviewed by a committee constituted by the Ministry. 

If approved, the organization will receive the grant in two installments. 

The first installment is released upon approval, while the second installment is contingent upon the completion of the establishment of the group home. 

The timeline for the establishment of a group home is typically within six months from the date of receiving the first installment. 

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is the primary implementing authority for the Gharaunda scheme. 

The contact details for the Ministry can be found on their official website. 

They provide a helpline for inquiries related to the scheme. 

The helpline number is 1800 11 2001. 

The Gharaunda scheme also emphasizes the importance of community participation. 

Local communities are encouraged to engage with the group homes to foster a sense of belonging and support. 

The scheme aims to promote social inclusion and reduce the stigma associated with disabilities. 

In addition to housing, the group homes will offer various services such as counseling, healthcare, and recreational activities. 

The residents will also receive vocational training to enhance their skills and promote self-sufficiency. 

This training will be tailored to the individual needs of the residents. 

The Gharaunda scheme is expected to significantly impact the lives of adults with disabilities. 

It aims to empower them by providing a safe and nurturing environment. 

The initiative aligns with the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. 

It seeks to uphold the rights and dignity of individuals with disabilities. 

The scheme is part of a larger framework of social welfare initiatives by the Indian government. 

These initiatives aim to create an inclusive society where individuals with disabilities can thrive. 

The Gharaunda scheme is also expected to create job opportunities for caregivers and support staff. 

This will contribute to the local economy and provide employment to many individuals. 

Monitoring and evaluation of the group homes will be conducted by the Ministry to ensure compliance with the scheme's objectives. 

Regular audits and assessments will be carried out to maintain quality standards. 

The scheme also encourages the use of technology to enhance the living conditions of the residents. 

Digital tools may be employed for skill development and educational purposes. 

The Gharaunda scheme is a step towards realizing the vision of an inclusive society in India. 

It reflects the government's commitment to improving the lives of persons with disabilities. 

The scheme is expected to foster a sense of community and belonging among the residents. 

By providing a supportive environment, the Gharaunda scheme aims to enhance the overall well-being of adults with disabilities. 

The initiative is a crucial part of India's efforts to meet the Sustainable Development Goals. 

It specifically addresses Goal 10 which focuses on reducing inequalities. 

The Gharaunda scheme represents a significant investment in the future of adults with disabilities in India. 

It is designed to empower individuals and promote their rights and dignity. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's dedication to social justice and equality. 

Overall, the Gharaunda-Group Home for Adults Scheme stands as a comprehensive approach to addressing the needs of adults with disabilities in India. 

It combines financial support with a focus on rehabilitation and social integration. 

This holistic approach is essential for fostering an inclusive society. 

The successful implementation of the Gharaunda scheme will depend on collaboration between government agencies and civil society organizations. 

Together, they can create a supportive ecosystem for adults with disabilities. 

This initiative is a critical step towards ensuring that every individual has the opportunity to lead a fulfilling life.
